questions.enonce_markdown:
Define the following terms:

(i) Biotechnology.

(ii) Genetically modified organisms (GMOs).

(iii) DNA profiling. *[6 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Biotechnology** *(2 marks)*: the **use of living organisms** (micro-organisms, plant or animal cells) **or their parts (such as enzymes) to make useful products or to carry out useful processes** for man. Examples: brewing, cheese and yoghurt making, antibiotic production, production of insulin by bacteria.

**(ii) Genetically modified organisms (GMOs)** *(2 marks)*: **organisms whose genetic material (DNA) has been altered by genetic engineering**, usually by **inserting a gene from another species** (a **transgene**) or by deleting or changing a gene. Examples: *Bt* maize (resistant to insects), golden rice, bacteria making human insulin.

**(iii) DNA profiling (genetic fingerprinting)** *(2 marks)*: a technique that **identifies an individual from the unique pattern of repeated sequences in his or her DNA**. DNA is extracted, **cut with restriction enzymes** (or amplified by PCR), the fragments are **separated by size by gel electrophoresis**, and the **pattern of bands** (detected with probes) is compared with that of other samples. Used in **forensic science, paternity tests, disease diagnosis and conservation**.

questions.enonce_markdown: Describe the main stages involved in penicillin production. *[6 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Penicillin** is a **secondary metabolite** made by the mould ***Penicillium chrysogenum*** in a **fed-batch culture** in a large, sterile, stainless-steel **fermenter**.

1. **Selection of a high-yielding strain and inoculum.** A high-yielding strain is chosen; its spores are grown in a series of small vessels to give enough **inoculum**.
2. **Preparation of the medium.** The **culture medium** contains a **carbon source** (**lactose**, which is used slowly, with **glucose** fed in small amounts), a **nitrogen source** (**corn steep liquor**), **mineral salts**, a **buffer** and a **precursor (phenylacetic acid)**. It is **sterilised** with steam to kill contaminants.
3. **Fermentation in the fermenter.** The medium is **inoculated** and the culture is kept under controlled conditions: **aerated** and **stirred** (the mould is aerobic), **temperature about 25 to 27 °C** (cooling jacket), **pH about 6.5 to 7** (acid or alkali added), antifoam added. There are **two phases**: a **growth phase (trophophase)**, in which the mould grows and makes little penicillin, then a **production phase (idiophase)**, in which, when a nutrient becomes limiting and glucose or lactose is **fed in slowly**, **penicillin is made**. It lasts about **6 to 8 days**.
4. **Extraction and recovery.** The **mycelium is filtered off**; the filtrate is **acidified** and the penicillin is extracted into an organic **solvent** (for example butyl acetate), then back into water, and **crystallised** as the **potassium or sodium salt**.
5. **Purification, quality control and formulation**: the product is dried, **tested for purity and activity**, and packaged. (Part of it may be converted chemically into **semi-synthetic penicillins**.)

questions.enonce_markdown: Give the advantages and disadvantages of genetic engineering. *[8 marks]* *(6, 6, 8 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Advantages** *(4 marks)*

1. **Large-scale, cheap production of human proteins and vaccines** by bacteria or yeast (**insulin, growth hormone, factor VIII, hepatitis B vaccine**), instead of extracting them from animals or donors.
2. **Gene therapy** can treat some inherited diseases (for example severe combined immunodeficiency); **DNA probes and DNA profiling** help **diagnose disease, solve crimes and settle paternity**.
3. **Improved crops and animals**: resistance to pests (*Bt* maize, cotton), to herbicides and to drought, **higher yield and nutritional value** (golden rice), so **more food** is produced.
4. **Faster and more precise** than conventional breeding, and genes can be transferred **between different species**; **bioremediation** (bacteria that clean up oil and wastes) and cleaner industrial enzymes.

**Disadvantages** *(4 marks)*

1. **Possible risks to human health**: allergies, toxins, spread of **antibiotic resistance marker genes**; the **long-term effects are not known**.
2. **Risks to the environment**: the **transgene may spread** to wild relatives (herbicide-resistant "superweeds"), **harm to non-target organisms** and loss of **biodiversity**; planting a few GM varieties reduces **genetic diversity**.
3. **Ethical, moral and religious objections** (interfering with nature, human cloning, "designer babies"), and a danger of **misuse** (biological weapons).
4. **Economic problems**: it is **expensive**, the seeds are **patented by a few companies**, so poor farmers become dependent; the results of the insertion of a gene **can be unpredictable** (it may disrupt other genes).
